summary: Retiring a script/binary that is cited as a re-derive command in an ALREADY-CLOSED bundle's sealed _cycle_receipt.md permanently breaks scripts/denominator_gate.py's figure-provenance gate for that citation, with no prior exemption mechanism -- deleting shape_engine_boundary.py and reach_gate.rs this epic broke 9 citations across 8 sealed SD-34/SD-35 receipts (files_checked=297, violations=9, first caught by a full bash scripts/verify.sh run). The doctrine tension: AGENTS.md rule 9 needs a resolvable command, but sealed historical receipts are explicitly not supposed to be hand-edited to say something different than what was actually run. Fixed structurally (not by editing the sealed receipts) by adding a small, reviewed RETIRED_SCRIPT_PATHS registry to denominator_gate.py -- same posture as the existing pi_substring_allowlist.py pattern -- that lets a citation to a script retired by a named, dated operator ruling still count as reachable, without widening what counts as reachable for anything not on that reviewed list. Re-verified: figure-provenance green (violations=0) after the fix. Worth carrying forward: any future tool retirement should check figure-provenance against the FULL docs/release/ history, not just the current bundle, before assuming a deletion is clean.

detected_by: a teammate (team-lead), who checked running processes, found the real verify.sh had already completed, and killed the stray loop
impact: A background wait loop (until ! pgrep -f 'bash scripts/verify.sh'; do sleep 30; done) matched its own shell's command line via pgrep -f -- the pattern argument itself contains the literal string it was searching for -- so it never exited even after the real verify.sh run had long finished, appearing to hang for hours
resolution: switched to polling a captured PID directly (kill -0 "$PID") instead of a pgrep pattern match, and bounded every subsequent wait to short foreground polling loops (<=9 min per Bash call) rather than an unbounded background wait+notify
summary: SD-36 Epic B: pgrep -f self-matched its own invocation, the exact hazard this repo's own memory already names ('pgrep wait loops must not match themselves'); root cause was not applying that known lesson
